propositions: A model class configured with provider "bedrock" and a canonical versioned Bedrock model id containing a colon has its explicit provider silently dropped, because _resolve_target treats any colon in the model string as already-provider-qualified.
Unversioned Bedrock aliases resolve correctly while canonical '...-v1:0' ids fail, so the versioned form is the majority AWS-published shape yet is broken.
Downstream infer_provider splits the unqualified id on its first colon and returns a fragment of the model id as the provider, which the provider factory rejects.
The operator-facing error reports 'unknown provider' naming most of the model id, contradicting the configured (and registered) 'bedrock' provider and misdirecting debugging.

The fix centralizes the qualified/unqualified decision into split_provider_qualifier, testing prefix shape (identifier, no dots) rather than mere colon presence, so both _resolve_target and infer_provider agree and no working config regresses.
Graceful fallback to a default provider is rejected because silent provider substitution defeats the epic's goal; the gate already fails closed and that behavior must remain unchanged.
